newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia may sign PGM decree next week - MOF.
newsitem.headline: Russia may sign PGM decree next week - MOF.

text.p: The Russian government may sign next week a decree outlining deliveries of platinum group metals to Japan, Vladimir Rybkin, the head of the Finance Ministry's precious metals section, said on Thursday.
"I think that the decree may be signed next week," he said in a telephone interview. "I think it is possible that there will be deliveries in May."
When queried, Rybkin gave no concrete reason why he thought the decree could materialise next week and supplies begin in May, saying only, "...because there are reasons to think this."
Resumption of exports hinge upon a document requiring Prime Minister Victor Chernomyrdin's signature.
When asked if the delays were connected to reserves levels, Rybkin declined to comment, saying the question was not for him.
A Russian official in Tokyo said on Monday that there would be no Russian shipments of platinum group metals to Japan in April and that May shipments were also in doubt.
Japan is the world's largest consumer of palladium and Russia the largest producer of the metal.

Contract talks are usually held in December for deliveries to begin in the next calendar year. Almazjuvelirexport, the state export agency, carries out the deliveries as stipulated in the government document.
